paragraphs: Hyman cites Yoma 76b for the reading given by Dikdukei Soferim: Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of R’ Pinchas of Tzippori. In the reading Hyman calls “our text,” the teacher is Rav Huna of Tzippori. Hyman reports that Yuchasin agreed with Dikdukei Soferim. Compare Yoma 77b.

notes.text: The alternative name abbreviated ר״ה remains unidentified. The bounded Yoma 76b check did not locate the quoted attribution.

The saved whole Davidson Yoma77b scalar explicitly has Rabbi Pinchas reporting Rav Huna of Tzippori. Supplied76b is retained beside77b; no printed numeral history is proved. This locally supports Huna for ר״ה and the reporter’s Rabbi title. The distinct Pinchas-of-Tzippori form is Hyman’s report of Dikdukei Soferim and Yuchasin, neither apparatus newly inspected, so its abbreviated title remains R'. The secondary Seder HaDorot search snippet is not independent adjudication or a fresh full witness. The name-originality and apparatus questions remain held.

Direct inspection of Dikdukei Soferim on Yoma, pp. 246–247, note ק, confirms that the apparatus gives Pinchas of Tzippori and expressly cites Yuchasin for that form. The printed-text column has Huna. The corresponding passage is in Yoma 77b in the Davidson edition, while Hyman printed 76b. The Tartu scan’s extracted text separately lists Rabbi Pinchas of Tzippori. This evidence leaves the priority of the readings open.
